_why: Corrected 2026-09-22. An earlier pass concluded these outlets had no Bluesky presence. That was wrong, and the cause was the search method: queries appended words like 'reporter' and 'congress' to the outlet name, which degraded matching instead of narrowing it. A bare outlet-name query, plus reading who the outlet's own account follows, found them immediately.
_method: Two probes, both cheap. 1) app.bsky.graph.getFollows on the outlet account, because outlets follow their own staff. 2) app.bsky.actor.searchActors with the bare outlet name, no qualifiers. Use both: The Hill's staff showed up only in follows, CQ Roll Call's only in search.

_findings.Punchbowl News: 5 current staff on Bluesky. No X needed.
_findings.The Hill: 7 current staff on Bluesky, including energy and environment. No X needed.
_findings.CQ Roll Call: 8 current staff on Bluesky, including energy, defense and the morning-brief writer. No X needed.
_findings.POLITICO: 11 current staff on Bluesky. No X needed.
_findings.The Daily Wire: Thin. Only a culture reporter and a co-founder host. Policy staff are on X.

_howToFill: Set the handle for each person, no @, then move the entry into roster.json with a weight. Never invent a handle: a wrong one silently polls the wrong account and bills you for it.
_costNote: About $0.005 per post read. One reporter posting 20 times a day is roughly $3/month. The list below is now short enough that X is a small line item rather than the main ingestion route.

outlets.why: Reads the politics of an energy or AI bill from the right. A tracker built only on mainstream coverage misses how a bill is being framed to a conservative audience.
Congressional enterprise reporting. Nothing found on Bluesky by either probe.
Some Pro-tier reporters post to X only. The free-tier ones are already covered on Bluesky.
